To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Recent model runs from the National Weather Service and ECMWF show a moderate marine layer with morning fog and onshore westerly flow of 10–20 mph limiting daytime warming, supporting the tight clustering around 68–71°F. Differentiation between the 68–69°F and 70–71°F bins hinges on subtle variables: depth of the marine inversion, timing of any partial clearing that allows brief solar heating, and exact wind speeds at the official KSFO station used for resolution. Stronger advection of 55–58°F ocean air favors the lower bin, while a shallower layer or lighter winds tilt toward the higher one. With no major heat-wave intrusion expected from inland valleys, probabilities reflect this narrow forecast spread rather than broad uncertainty.

eventMetadata.context_description: A strong cold front and associated upper trough are driving cooler, windy conditions across the Western Cape, yet latest model runs and observational data point to a moderating maritime influence that should produce a daily maximum near 19°C in Cape Town on August 11. Trader sentiment, reflected in the 56.5% implied probability for 19°C and 26% for 20°C, incorporates recent South African Weather Service guidance and ensemble consensus showing limited recovery from the front’s passage, with wind speeds and cloud cover capping further rises. Historical analogs for similar August systems rarely exceed 20°C, reinforcing the narrow distribution around these outcomes ahead of final observational confirmation.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Qingdao Jiaodong International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 11 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Qingdao Jiaodong International Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/cn/qingdao/ZSQD.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Coastal sea breezes and expected light rain or afternoon thunderstorms are key moderating factors that limit daytime heating, while high humidity and variable cloud cover add uncertainty to exact peak readings. Recent cooling from early-August heat in Shandong supports this range, with official guidance indicating no strong high-pressure dominance. Traders appear to emphasize ensemble model agreement and historical late-summer patterns, where small shifts in steering winds or precipitation timing could tip the highest temperature between 30°C and 31°C.

eventMetadata.context_description: Ensemble forecasts from Météo-France and the ECMWF currently favor a transient high-pressure ridge over northern France, promoting mostly sunny skies, light winds, and efficient daytime heating that supports afternoon maxima near 34–36 °C in central Paris on August 12. Model consensus places the most likely peak in the mid-30s, aligning with the market’s heaviest volume on 35 °C (47.5 %) and 34 °C (30.5 %), while the smaller probabilities on 36–37 °C reflect residual uncertainty in exact ridge timing and any late marine-air intrusion. Updated runs expected within 24–48 hours will refine these ranges ahead of resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecast models from agencies like the Pakistan Meteorological Department indicate Karachi's August 12 maximum temperature will likely settle near 32–33°C amid below-normal monsoon rainfall and persistent high humidity from Arabian Sea moisture. These conditions moderate daytime heating through cloud cover and evaporative cooling while steering patterns limit extreme advection of hot air from the northwest. Subtle differences between 32°C and 33°C outcomes hinge on short-term variables such as boundary-layer mixing, local sea-breeze timing, and any late intensification of the seasonal low over Balochistan. Traders weigh ensemble consensus showing limited day-to-day variability against the potential for clearer skies to push readings slightly higher, consistent with climatological August averages of 31–32°C. Updated model runs expected in the next 24–48 hours will refine these probabilities.
